Same-type selectivity: PRMT5 IC50 500 nM (one document) against DOT1L IC50 0.4 nM = 1250-fold, from different documents and assays, so an indication and not a measured window; PRMT7 IC50 7500 nM; PRMT5-MEP50 complex IC50 >20000 nM. assay_nature: Biochemical (radiometric, SPR) and cell assays. The only neural-relevant cell concentrations found are in the colorectal lines of PMID 31888761: 30-70 uM to move viability and MYC, four to five orders above the biochemical IC50; the exposure used in human NPCs (PMID 38297124) was not found in the text served
foundation: Selective, potent DOT1L catalytic inhibitor (abstract of PMID 21741596: selective killing of MLL-translocated cells, little effect on others). The chain needs DOT1L to keep MYC protein up. Support for that sign exists in colorectal cancer lines (PMID 31888761, read: EPZ004777 and DOT1L knockdown lowered c-Myc RNA and protein, H3K79me2 on the MYC promoter, MYC rescue restored proliferation). Abstract-level only: prostate (PMID 32814769) and myeloma (PMID 30171029) papers from the PubMed search, not read
decisive_assumption: That EPZ004777 lowers MYC protein in WWOX-deficient radial glia through DOT1L, and that this lowers progenitor retention without lowering neuronal output (the second half is unmeasured: SATB2 is already low in the KO)
counter_evidence: (1) The edge's only SIGNOR reference (PMID 26199140, read, partial full text) says verbatim 'DOT1L did not change the total level of c-Myc expression': the relation there is DOT1L-MYC-p300 co-binding on EMT-TF promoters in breast epithelial cells, with EPZ004777 reversing the EMT-TF readout, not MYC. IT9 had already called the edge co-binding; reading the reference confirms it. (2) Sign is context-split, not refuted: colorectal lines show lowering (L4). No measurement of DOT1L -> MYC exists in any neural cell. (3) Neural requirement for DOT1L: genetic Dot1l loss in mouse telencephalon reduces PAX6 progenitors and SATB2 neurons (PMID 30329130, read in part); inhibition or knockdown impairs proliferation and survival of cortical NSCs through ATF4-DDIT3 ER stress (PMID 26299268, abstract); human monoallelic DOT1L loss-of-function variants cause a neurodevelopmental disorder (PMID 40494548, abstract). (4) A counter-signal in the other direction, so the net is mixed: transient EPZ004777 in human NPCs primed neurons to mature faster (PMID 38297124, read in part), which is not a MYC readout. (5) Locally MYCN is 5-7x more abundant than MYC in the organoid; which MYC the seed antibody sees is UNVERIFIED. (6) Potency gap in cells (30-70 uM v 0.4 nM) leaves a selectivity question in a cell, where PRMT5 (500 nM) and other targets are in reach
next_test: Step 0 of the hand-over first (matched-maturity wild-type radial glia MYC fraction; neuronal output after a MYC-axis lever). Compound step only if step 0 supports the role: in WWOX-deficient and corrected human NPC/organoid, EPZ004777 over a titration (including the nM range that lowers H3K79me2) versus a second chemotype (SGC0946 or pinometostat as alternatives, not as new evidence) versus DOT1L knockdown; read H3K79me2 (engagement), MYC and MYCN protein by cell class, MKI67/SOX2/SATB2 fractions, and ATF4/DDIT3 as the stress control
result_that_would_change_the_decision: MYC protein falling with DOT1L inhibition at H3K79me2-engaging concentrations, reproduced by DOT1L knockdown, with progenitor fraction and SATB2 neurons not falling, would move it to KEPT_CONDITIONAL; no MYC change, or ATF4-DDIT3 induction with progenitor loss, would reject H_HARM for this axis

question_arm: Q6 H_HARM (lower MYC / progenitor retention), chain AURKB -> MYC
mechanism_cluster_and_seed_origin: AURKB -P(+)-> MYC [SIGNOR; ProtMapper text mining of the same paper; one reference: PMID 32049046]; seed S101 MYC up (protein, human, tier A, PMID 42397075), ONE origin counted once; cluster of 37 Aurora-kinase alternatives (barasertib, AMG-900, AT-9283, ...) shares the chain: one mechanism, not independent support

assay_nature: Biochemical enzyme assays (Aurora B/INCENP and Aurora A/TPX2 complexes), kinobeads chemoproteomics (lysate), cancer-cell proliferation (EC50 40-500 nM) and phospho-histone H3 / polyploidy readouts (abstract). No neural cell assay
foundation: Multitargeted Aurora B inhibitor with documented cellular engagement (H3 phosphorylation suppressed, polyploidy; PMID 23358665 abstract). Edge reference (PMID 32049046, read in part): AURKB phosphorylates MYC at S67, counteracts GSK3b/FBXW7 degradation; AURKB knockdown or AZD1152 lowers MYC protein (half-life 30 to 15 min; 40 to 18 min) with unchanged mRNA, in T-ALL cells
decisive_assumption: That TAK-901 lowers MYC protein in WWOX-deficient radial glia through AURKB-dependent stabilisation, separable from the mitotic failure that Aurora B inhibition itself causes
counter_evidence: (1) The edge reference tested AZD1152 (barasertib), never TAK-901, in T-ALL and a few leukaemia lines; Jurkat and PEER were resistant with MYC unchanged, and a MYC fall was required for response, with functional FBXW7 predicting it (L12-L14). (2) The same paper states regulation is of c-MYC and not N-MYC (neuroblastoma, L11); neural progenitors lean on MYCN (organoid MYCN 5-7x MYC), so transfer to radial glia is unshown. (3) Aurora B inhibition causes polyploidy and cell-cycle failure in dividing cells at 40-500 nM (PMID 23358665): in a progenitor culture a lower MYC-positive fraction could reflect cell loss, not MYC lowering; this is the carried barasertib liability (cytotoxicity in the very cells to be preserved), and it is a class property shown in this molecule's own paper. (4) Attribution to AURKB is not separable from AURKA (1.4-fold) and the compound hits dozens of kinases under 1 uM, so a genetic AURKB control is mandatory. (5) Microcephaly literature ties AURKB-containing mitotic machinery to progenitor survival (title-level only, not used as evidence)
next_test: Step 0 of the hand-over first. Compound step only if step 0 supports the role: WWOX-deficient and corrected human NPC/organoid, TAK-901 at 10-100 nM versus a more AURKB-selective compound (barasertib/AZD2811 as comparator, no ranking assumed) versus AURKB knockdown, reading MYC and MYCN protein half-life (cycloheximide chase), p-S67 MYC if an antibody works, histone H3 pS10 (engagement), ploidy, caspase and cell counts in the same wells, so that MYC lowering can be separated from cell loss
result_that_would_change_the_decision: MYC half-life shortening with AURKB-dependence at concentrations that leave ploidy and cell counts unchanged would move it to KEPT_CONDITIONAL; MYC fraction falling only together with polyploidy or cell loss, or no change in MYC half-life, would reject the arm for this molecule

question_arm: Q8 H_HARM ('NRF2 tone': raise NRF2 tone; role of the observed change unknown), chain AHR -> NFE2L2; guard NRF2_TONE_UNRESOLVED (evaluation forbidden on it)
mechanism_cluster_and_seed_origin: AHR -T(+)-> NFE2L2 [CollecTRI / ExTRI / Pavlidis, 35 distinct references listed; the classical one is PMID 15790560]; seed S132 / N22-A001 NFE2L2 down (expression, human, tier A): organoid KO/WT mean CPM 0.75 (4 v 2 libraries), hNSC and neurons lower in a second system (one library per arm); ONE origin (shared IT7 derivation of GSE156243 and GSE126075). Cluster: TCDD only (alternative AhR agonist, no typed value). IT21P2-1009 is the DGIdb twin of the same substance (counted once)
identity_form_state: ChEMBL CHEMBL259571, small molecule, max phase 4 (first approval 2022, topical cream; ChEMBL topical flag true, oral/parenteral false), ATC D05AX07, curated mechanism AhR agonist (3 references), InChIKey ZISJNXNHJRQYJO-CMDGGOBGSA-N; C17H18O2; VERIFIED (ChEMBL REST 2026-11-03; US label via DailyMed set id 9309d20f-8cd4-4c96-93fa-7f730e83c7ab, SPL version 4, 2025-07-30)
target_action_potency_selectivity: AhR agonist: ChEMBL EC50 13-27 nM (4 values, 4 documents, human HepG2-Lucia AhR DRE-luciferase reporter, 24 h): a reporter potency, not a binding constant. Guide to Pharmacology: no ligand/affinity row for tapinarof (attribution not assessable there); the only AHR value in the typed release is ezutromid (an antagonist, Kd 50 nM), and TCDD has no typed value, so class_alternatives_ahr.tsv allows no potency comparison and none is made. The primary paper (PMID 28595996, abstract) shows AhR dependence of the anti-inflammatory effect in mice. No data on NRF2 or KEAP1 binding
assay_nature: Cell reporter assays (HepG2), human skin cells and mouse skin in vivo (abstract); keratinocyte NRF2/HO-1 induction (abstract of PMID 40945864; title of PMID 37838333). No neural cell datum for tapinarof
foundation: AhR agonism is established (primary paper, label). AHR activation raises NRF2 transcript through XRE-like elements in the Nrf2 promoter and is lost on AHR knockdown (PMID 15790560, abstract; TCDD). Tapinarof activates the NRF2 arm in human keratinocytes (HO-1; PMID 40945864, abstract) and, in microglia, an AhR agonist (FICZ, not tapinarof) raised Nrf2 DNA-binding under LPS (PMC12210381, read in part, L15-L16)
decisive_assumption: That in WWOX-deficient human neural cells tapinarof raises NFE2L2 (and NRF2 activity) through AHR, and that a higher NRF2 tone is the beneficial direction (the role of the lower NFE2L2 transcript is unknown: the seed has no protein, nuclear NRF2, NQO1 activity or ROS datum in any WWOX-deficient mammalian neural system, and NQO1 and G6PD move the other way in the second system)
counter_evidence: (1) Role unresolved by design (guard NRF2_TONE_UNRESOLVED; rival: NRF2 protein/nuclear localisation/NQO1 activity does not differ once maturity and clone are matched). (2) Mouse MEFs carry Nfe2l2 and Nqo1 transcripts HIGHER in Wwox-null cells (one sample per genotype, supplement not opened) and organoid HMOX1, SRXN1, GSR, MAFG run up while SLC7A11, BACH1 run down: a mixed signature. (3) Locally the AhR axis is not obviously silent: AHRR, an AhR-target repressor, is 3.0x higher in KO organoid (28.1/27.7/24.9/16.8 v 9.4/6.7 cpm) and CYP1A1 2.5x (0.9-5.3 cpm, near the noise floor), while NFE2L2 is 0.75x; AHR itself is 3.3-6.0 cpm in organoid and ABSENT from the hNPC table. Descriptive, 4 v 2, composition-confounded; it suggests AHR -> NFE2L2 is not what sets NFE2L2 in this system. (4) Tapinarof NRF2 activation may be AhR-independent: the molecule is a redox-active stilbene that scavenges radicals (PMID 39067626, abstract) and is unstable in aqueous medium (about 50% lost in 48 h at pH 7.4), so a multi-day neural culture dose is uncertain. (5) AhR activation is adverse in neural systems in the TCDD literature: it slows NPC proliferation (G1 arrest, PMID 20486776, abstract), impairs adult hippocampal neurogenesis (both AhR deletion and TCDD; PMID 23240617, abstract), disrupts embryonic zebrafish brain (PMID 36523606, abstract); TCDD is persistent and tapinarof is rapidly metabolised (label; HaCaT sulfates and glucuronides), so this does not transfer without a measurement, but the direction of risk is toward the progenitor and neurogenesis axis that matters for a developmental epileptic encephalopathy. (6) Systemic route: see feasibility
next_test: Step 0 of the hand-over first (nuclear NRF2 and KEAP1 protein, NQO1 activity, a ROS reporter at baseline and after an oxidative challenge in isogenic WWOX-deficient v corrected neural cultures; card L01 step 0, NEED-REDOX-NRF2). Compound step only if the role is shown to be insufficient NRF2 tone: tapinarof (freshly prepared, re-dosed to offset instability, 10-100 nM bracketing the reporter EC50) v AHR knockdown / CH223191 v NFE2L2 knockdown v a non-AhR NRF2 activator (KEAP1-directed) as comparator, reading NFE2L2, NQO1, HMOX1 and CYP1A1/AHRR (AhR engagement) in the same wells plus proliferation and SOX2/MKI67 fractions as the adverse-effect read
result_that_would_change_the_decision: NRF2 activity raised by tapinarof only with AHR present and abolished by NFE2L2 knockdown, with proliferation unchanged, keeps it conditional; NRF2 unchanged by tapinarof, or raised without AHR (redox route), or proliferation/neuronal differentiation impaired at AhR-engaging concentrations, rejects the arm as written. If step 0 shows NRF2 tone is not low, the arm closes without a compound step

feasibility_note_exposure: Topical drug. US label (read): plasma below the 50 pg/mL limit in 68% of samples in adults with extensive psoriasis, Day 1 Cmax 0.90 +/- 1.4 ng/mL falling to 0.12 on Day 29; children 2 years and older Day 1 Cmax 2.4 +/- 3.9 ng/mL (youngest group 3.8), BQL in 76% on Day 28; plasma protein binding about 99%; hepatic oxidation, glucuronidation and sulfation; contraindications none. The paediatric maximal-use trial (abstract) reports mean Cmax 2.44 ng/mL, about 9.6 nM total plasma at MW 254, the same order as the reporter EC50 (13-27 nM) but with 99% protein binding, so free exposure is far lower; no CNS or brain-penetration measurement exists in anything retrieved (UNKNOWN, not negative); a review's statement of 'localized exposure' is a claim. Rat subcutaneous studies: no tapinarof-related effects on offspring neurobehaviour up to 30 mg/kg/day (label, reproductive study); juvenile-rat renal pelvic dilatation at 15 mg/kg/day. So a systemic or CNS route is unsupported; the only feasible use is in vitro or ex vivo, and the label gives no basis for a CNS indication
